subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which material is most suitable for bending into a flowing linear 3D form?
questions.explain: Wire is easily bent and twisted, making it ideal for linear, gestural 3D forms.

questions.q: 'Hierarchy' in a layout means...
options: Arranging elements so the most important information stands out first
questions.explain: Visual hierarchy uses size, weight and position to guide the eye to the most important content first.

questions.q: Wool is a natural fibre obtained from...
questions.explain: Wool is a natural animal fibre sheared from the fleece of sheep.

questions.q: Felting makes fabric by...
options: Matting and pressing fibres together with moisture and friction
questions.explain: Felting binds loose fibres into a fabric by pressing them with moisture, heat and friction.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Colours that sit directly opposite each other
Colours that sit next to each other
Different tones of the same hue
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

questions.q: Which textile designer is famous for nature-inspired patterns of the Arts and Crafts movement?
questions.explain: William Morris designed richly patterned, nature-based textiles and wallpapers in the Arts and Crafts style.

questions.q: 'Welding' is a construction method used mainly with...
questions.explain: Welding fuses pieces of metal together using heat, a common method in metal sculpture.

questions.q: What does the 'white balance' setting on a camera adjust?
options: The colour cast so whites appear neutral under different lighting
questions.explain: White balance corrects colour casts so that whites look neutral under different light sources.

questions.q: A 'design brief' usually sets out...
options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

questions.q: A 'mock-up' in graphic design is...
options: A trial version showing how a design will look
A finished printed product for sale
questions.explain: A mock-up is a realistic preview that shows how the final design will appear before production.

questions.q: Oil paint is mixed and thinned using...
options: Solvents such as turpentine or linseed oil
questions.explain: Oil paint is oil-based and is thinned and cleaned with solvents like turpentine, not water.

questions.q: Photographing a subject from directly above is known as a...
questions.explain: A bird's-eye or flat-lay viewpoint looks straight down on the subject from above.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: RGB (red, green, blue) is the additive light model used by screens and digital devices.

questions.q: The Renaissance saw a renewed interest in...
questions.explain: Renaissance artists revived classical ideals and developed realism and linear perspective.

questions.q: Block printing on fabric works by...
options: Pressing an inked carved block onto the cloth
questions.explain: Block printing presses a raised, inked carved block onto fabric to repeat a motif.

questions.q: What is 'stippling'?
options: Building tone using many small dots
questions.explain: Stippling builds up tone and texture using numerous small dots placed close together.

questions.q: A 'vector' image is one that...
options: Uses mathematical paths so it scales without losing quality
Can only be black and white
Is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged
questions.explain: Vector graphics use mathematical paths, so they can be scaled to any size without pixelation.

questions.q: A 'photogram' is made by...
options: Placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light
questions.explain: A photogram is a cameraless image made by laying objects on photographic paper and exposing it to light.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

questions.q: A serif font is one that has...
options: Small lines or 'feet' at the ends of letters
questions.explain: Serif fonts have small finishing strokes (serifs) at the ends of letters; sans-serif fonts do not.

questions.q: What is 'visual' (or implied) texture?
options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.
